verdict.summary: Create the app and switch on public distribution, with no review. A Slack Marketplace listing is optional and slow (10+ installs first, then up to about 10 weeks).

whoYouNeed.role: A member of a Slack workspace you control
whoYouNeed.why: Every Slack app is created inside one workspace, and you test it there first.

steps.title: Sign in to Slack's app dashboard
steps.plain: Log in at api.slack.com/apps with the workspace that will own the app.
steps.whyHuman: Signing in is yours to do.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.plain: Click Create New App, choose 'From scratch', give it a name and pick the workspace that owns it.

evidence.note: The exact button labels come from Slack's dashboard, not the page cited. Not checked by hand yet.

steps.title: Add the redirect address and the permissions
steps.plain: Under OAuth & Permissions, paste the redirect address from your Composio Slack auth config, then add the permissions your agent needs.
steps.technical: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS and cannot contain '#'. Bot scopes and user scopes are listed separately. Composio's auth config lists the scopes it requests.

steps.title: Switch on public distribution
steps.plain: Without this, only your own workspace can install the app. Open Manage Distribution, tick off Slack's checklist, and click Activate Public Distribution.
steps.technical: Checklist requires OAuth handling and HTTPS on every request URL. No review happens at this step.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.plain: From Basic Information, copy the client ID and client secret into your Composio Slack auth config.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is a password for your app. Pasting it yourself keeps it out of any agent's chat history.

steps.title: Install in a second workspace to test
steps.plain: Connect a different workspace through Composio to confirm other teams can install it.

evidence.note: Slack asks Marketplace applicants to test outside the development workspace. We apply the same advice here.

forks.condition: You want a listing in the Slack Marketplace
forks.effect: You first need 10 or more active workspace installs. Then a preliminary review (up to 10 business days) and a functional review (up to 10 weeks for new apps), with a demo video and test credentials.

forks.condition: Your customer's workspace requires admin approval for apps
forks.effect: The user who connects can only request the app. Their workspace admin must approve it, so expect a short wait on the customer side.

nuances.title: The redirect address must be HTTPS
nuances.detail: Slack rejects plain http:// redirect addresses, including for local testing.
nuances.ifStuck: Use Composio's HTTPS redirect address, or a tunnel such as ngrok for local work.

nuances.title: Ask for fewer permissions
nuances.detail: Workspace admins weigh the permissions you request when deciding whether to approve your app.
nuances.ifStuck: Remove scopes your agent does not use yet. You can add them later.

config.redirectUriNote: Use the HTTPS redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config.

scopes.name: channels:history
scopes.plain: Read messages in public channels the app is in.
